Maya Chen: quick q — for the bulk-edit form (5+ inputs) do we go inline-errors-only, or inline + an error summary banner listing fields? also debating confirmation copy for destructive bulk ops (typed 'DELETE' vs typed resource name). thoughts? Ben Park: my vote: inline for field-level, + small persistent summary at top for bulk submit failures. summary should be actionable (links). Sam Ortiz: +1. Summary helps when errors are spread across collapsed sections. we should also make each summary item keyboard-focusable and move focus to the first invalid field when clicked. Anya Li: accessibility nit — summary must have role="alert" or aria-live? If we auto-focus it, screen reader will announce it. also ensure error links use focus management rather than jump to prevent keyboard users losing context. Maya Chen: agree. proposal: - show inline errors under each field (short copy) - when submit fails and >1 error, show dismissible summary banner with a list of field labels as buttons - clicking an item focuses field and opens collapsed section if needed - banner gets aria-live="assertive" on failure, but buttons manage focus when activated Luis Gomez: copy for bulk-delete: typed confirmation is safer but annoying for users. for >100 items maybe require typed name, otherwise a single-step modal with a checkbox + "I understand"? thoughts on thresholds? Ben Park: threshold is fine. also consider rate-limiting typed confirmations: if action is reversible (soft-delete) we can go lighter. For permanent deletes, typed confirmation (DELETE) is okay. We should standardize copy: "Type DELETE to permanently delete N items." Sam Ortiz: can we auto-populate the typed string in a visually-hidden input for screen readers? might be weird. prefer explicit visible input. also ensure the confirm input has aria-label and error messaging. Anya Li: accessibility checklist for the pattern: - error summary has role="status" or aria-live=assertive - summary list items are
Project name can't be blank
``` Ben Park: that looks good. we should also include a visually-hidden summary heading for screen readers: "You have 3 errors" (h2.sr-only). Luis Gomez: for the typed confirm modal copy — suggestion: "This will permanently delete 34 projects. This action cannot be undone. Type DELETE to confirm." add hint under input: "You can cancel with Esc or click Cancel." Sam Ortiz: small UX thing — if user opens modal on keyboard, focus should land in the input, but we must expose the cancel button next in tab order. don't trap keyboard. Maya Chen: ok action items: - Sam/Ben to prototype inline+summary interactions and keyboard flow (jump-to-error, focus restore) — due Wed - Anya to write a11y acceptance criteria and test cases (screenreader flows, aria attributes) — due Thu - Luis to draft copy variations for typed vs checkbox confirm + threshold suggestions — due Fri design-bot: accessibility-linter ran on current branch: 5 warnings (missing aria-describedby on 2 fields, modal focus trap misconfigured). See CI link: https://ci.redwood.dev/1234 Maya Chen: thanks — will address linter items in the prototype PR. any dissent on inline+summary approach? Ben Park: none from me. fine to ship as experiment behind flag. :+1: Anya Li: sounds good. i'll prepare a small screenreader script to validate once prototype is up. Luis Gomez: fine — will share copy variants in a thread in #marketing later. Maya Chen: great, closing this thread. will post the prototype link when ready. :sparkles:
